arguments.body: Hi Amelia, thanks for telling us. A rotten-egg smell from a boiler can mean a gas leak, so please treat it as urgent tonight. Please: 1) Don't use switches, flames or the boiler. 2) Open windows and doors. 3) Get everyone out of the flat, including your flatmate's mum, and wait outside. 4) Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 (free, 24 hours) from outside. If anyone feels unwell or it's an immediate danger, call 999. We're sending a Gas Safe engineer and our team has been alerted. Please don't go back in until the gas engineer says it's safe. Please reply once you're out safe.

answers.question: 1. Severity and why?
answers.answer: Emergency. A rotten-egg smell at a gas boiler is a suspected gas leak whatever the tenant says; an 82-year-old is also in the flat. The tenant's 'not urgent' and 'not too early' don't change that.

answers.question: 2. What do you tell the tenant, in order?
answers.answer: Don't use switches, flames or the boiler; open windows; everyone leaves including the elderly visitor; call 0800 111 999 from outside; 999 if anyone is unwell or in danger; engineer is being sent; don't re-enter until cleared; reply when out safe.

answers.question: 3. Actions tonight?

arguments.body: Hi Amelia, thanks for telling us. A rotten-egg smell from a boiler can mean a gas leak, so please treat it as urgent tonight. Please: 1) Don't use switches, flames or the boiler. 2) Open windows and doors. 3) Get everyone out of the flat, including your flatmate's mum, and wait outside. 4) Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 (free, 24 hours) from outside. If anyone feels unwell or it's an immediate danger, call 999. We're sending a Gas Safe engineer and our team has been alerted. Please don't go back in until the gas engineer says it's safe. Please reply once you're out safe.
